1: The patient's symptoms and the location of the mass are consistent with a Canal of Nuck hernia, which is a rare condition where a hernia occurs through the inguinal canal and into the labia majora.

The patient's symptoms of a painless right vulvar mass extending into the right inguinal region, with gradual enlargement over the past four months, are consistent with a Canal of Nuck hernia. The ultrasound findings of a well-defined, hypoechoic solid mass measuring 90 × 44 × 55 mm in the right labia majora tracking into the inguinal canal also support this diagnosis.
